what: Rows of character cells flip picture frames together on one beat (default 227ms). The sequence table 0·0·1·1·2·2·3·3 makes each frame stay two beats, giving a choppy stop-motion dance, and only cells with data-odd follow another sequence (0·1·3·2·0·1·3·2) on the off-beat so they look like a hidden one. The beat number is written only on the root (--fx-k·--fx-k-odd) and the vertical strip inside each cell is a sprite that shifts up by that much, so there is no blur or curve in between

options.seq: Section numbers shown for each beat (space separated), default ”0 0 1 1 2 2 3 3”
options.odd: Order table for data-odd cells, default same as seq — the original hidden one ‹0 1 3 2 0 1 3 2›
options.[data-fx-part]: Two types: ① unit (window sized to one picture) > strip (vertical band) > frame (image frames, top to bottom) ② lay only the background sprite (frames stacked vertically) on the unit — background-position shifts by --fx-h each step. The consumer may relay the cells to fit the window size (the frame count is a root variable so there is nothing to look up again)
options.--fx-h: Height of one frame in a background sprite (css variable), default 112px — if the cell has no strip and frames are stacked vertically in the background, the background position shifts by this much each step (original type)

use: Pose 1Pose 2Pose 3Pose 4…
note: The original swaps classes u_0 to u_7 on the footer every 227ms, and each class picks the cell’s background sprite position (0·-112·-224·-336px). The part likewise edits only one root per beat and the cells follow through css variables — editing each cell would trigger style recalculation as many times as there are cells.
